key_insight: Allowing a small finite training error changes the geometry of non-convex neural network solutions: dense, accessible regions can survive beyond the zero-temperature OGP threshold, and may still generalize well.
engineering_relevance: This suggests that controlled thermal noise or finite-loss optimization may help training algorithms escape frozen, hard-to-reach minima in overconstrained neural models.
method: Extended the zero-temperature frozen 1RSB analysis to finite temperature.
Derived a criterion based on smoothness of the single-pattern Gibbs weight near the decision boundary.
Generalized the overlap gap property to finite energy and tested a finite-energy message-passing algorithm numerically.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports both analytical threshold results and numerical message-passing experiments showing that thermal noise enables effective generalization in regimes where zero-error recovery is computationally hard.
watch_item: The finite-temperature benefits depend on model-specific geometry and the smoothness of the loss near the decision boundary, so the effect may not transfer uniformly to other architectures or loss functions.
paper_title: On the robustness of noisy solutions in non-convex neural networks
